source.title: MentorNet: Learning Data-Driven Curriculum for Very Deep Neural Networks on Corrupted Labels
source.authors: Lu Jiang; Zheng-Yuan Zhou; Thomas Leung; Li-Jia Li; Li Fei-Fei

record.tranche_reason: Tests deep CNN performance under controlled corrupted labels using a learned curriculum and reports comparisons across corruption fractions; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for fitting completely corrupted labels. Its own controlled experiments use noise fractions 0.2, 0.4, and 0.8; Table 2 reports validation accuracy, while Figure 3 describes a near-zero weighted training error for MentorNet at one setting. Values used only to select hyperparameters and results cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The standard FullModel baseline uses the original label-corruption procedure and reports validation accuracy across corruption fractions. Section 5.1 also explicitly reports zero training error on corrupted data in the Figure 3 experiment. These results bear on V4, although most experiments evaluate a mitigation method.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase correctly describes the main conclusion: MentorNet improves generalization on controlled and real-world noisy labels. However, the authors also report their own Figure 3 result as consistent with zero training error on corrupted data. MentorNet's particular near-zero quantity is weighted loss and must not be described as perfect fitting of all training labels.
record.recipe_differences: Uses MentorNet curriculum and weighted training objectives; controlled experiments use partial label corruption rather than fully random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, noise fraction, StudentNet architecture, and curriculum method change reported validation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: MentorNet improves clean validation accuracy under controlled label corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned sample weighting can improve generalization when training labels are partially corrupted.

fits_no_version.finding: Regularization variants yield different ImageNet validation accuracies at 40% corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization choices affect generalization under partial label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: MentorNet's weighted training loss approaches zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The learned weighted objective converges; this does not establish fitting every corrupted label.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 35th ICML, PMLR 80, 2018
record.problems: The controlled-label tables report validation accuracy, not training error; Figure 3 gives only a textual description for one weighted-error setting. The study's own controlled experiments stop at 80% noise, and several relevant comparisons involve the added MentorNet curriculum.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 values for Forgetting, Self-paced, Focal Loss, Reed Soft, and MentorNet PD are omitted; the selected FullModel and MentorNet DD rows retain the baseline and learned-curriculum results across both datasets and noise fractions. Table 3 comparisons and Table 5 real-world noisy-label results are omitted because they do not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error under that labeling, and chance test performance with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time ratio between true and random labels, and convergence slowdown as corruption fraction increases.

The fully random endpoint, a continuous noise sweep, and perfect training fit across all tested fractions and architectures. The explicit standard-baseline training-fit evidence concerns resnet-101 on CIFAR-100 at 40% corruption.
Whether explicit regularization prevents fitting completely random labels, and whether removing it alone causes poor generalization on clean training labels.
Separate learning trajectories for genuine patterns and corrupted labels. Curriculum weights and aggregate training curves do not establish their temporal ordering.

missing.what: FullModel's training trajectory on CIFAR-100 at 40% corruption, including the authors' explicit statement that standard CNN training reaches zero training error. Preserve the distinction between ordinary baseline loss and MentorNet's weighted loss; exact plotted endpoint values are unavailable in the supplied text.

Clean-label resnet-101 baselines: training accuracy 1.00 on both CIFAR datasets, with validation accuracy 0.96 on CIFAR-10 and 0.79 on CIFAR-100. These supply the zero-corruption endpoint for the validation trend.
Inception FullModel validation accuracies across 0.2, 0.4 and 0.8 corruption: CIFAR-100 0.43, 0.38, 0.15; CIFAR-10 0.76, 0.73, 0.42. These provide an additional architecture's degradation trend.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Table 2; clean baselines in Table 1

record.verdict_notes: Table 2's CIFAR dataset assignments are reversed throughout R1–R12; Table 3 and the clean baselines corroborate the correction. Observed states for validation rows apply only to V4's measured degradation component. No failure of an untested component is inferred.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment with completely random labels or the original unmodified training setup is reported; the near-zero training-error statement concerns MentorNet's weighted error at 40% noise.
Training-time cost relative to true-label training and convergence time across corruption fractions are not reported.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.

Validation accuracy is reported at three nonzero noise fractions, but the study does not report perfect training fit across those fractions or a smooth test-error trajectory from no noise through fully random labels.
ImageNet comparisons include regularization variants at 40% noise, but do not test completely random labels or whether removing regularization alone harms generalization on true labels.
The study does not measure whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
